question: What unit of measurement is commonly used to express dietary energy?
explanation: Dietary energy is measured in kilocalories, which are commonly called calories on food labels and in clinical practice. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T006#GNS227_U4_T006_h1)

question: When does a patient maintain a stable body weight?

options.B: Energy intake drops to zero for a day
options.D: Energy expenditure is higher than energy intake

explanation: Weight remains stable when the total calories consumed match the total calories burned by the body. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T006#GNS227_U4_T006_h1)

question: Which macronutrient provides the highest number of calories per gram?
explanation: Fats are the most energy-dense nutrient, supplying nine kilocalories for every single gram consumed. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T006#GNS227_U4_T006_h2)

question: Why are dietary fats considered energy-dense?

options.A: They contain no carbon or hydrogen atoms
options.B: They convert directly into muscle without breakdown
options.C: They are digested much faster than carbs
options.D: They supply more than double the calories per gram compared to carbs or protein

explanation: You've got this! Fats give you nine calories per gram, while proteins and carbs only give four. That means fats pack much more energy into a smaller amount. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T006#GNS227_U4_T006_h2)

question: What is the largest component of total daily energy expenditure for most people?
explanation: Keeping your internal organs alive and functioning at rest takes up the vast majority of the calories you burn daily. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T006#GNS227_U4_T006_h3)

question: What does the 'thermic effect of food' mean?

options.A: Energy used to process and digest food
options.B: Heat produced when standing in cold weather
options.C: Calories burned during a heavy gym workout
options.D: Energy stored in fat tissue during starvation

explanation: Think of it this way: eating and digesting food actually makes your body work! The energy spent handling that food process is the thermic effect of food. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T006#GNS227_U4_T006_h3)

question: What body tissue is the primary driver of a person's metabolic rate?
explanation: Muscle tissue burns significantly more calories at rest than fat tissue, making muscle mass the main driver of metabolism. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T006#GNS227_U4_T006_h4)

question: Why do adult males typically have a higher resting metabolic rate than females of the same size?

options.A: Their digestive tract is physically longer
options.B: Their baseline body temperature is higher
options.C: Their brains require more glucose hourly
options.D: They generally have a higher percentage of lean muscle mass

explanation: Great job thinking through this! Men naturally tend to have more muscle mass than women, and since muscle burns more calories at rest, their baseline calorie need is higher. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T006#GNS227_U4_T006_h4)

question: Which macronutrient requires the most energy for the body to digest and process?
explanation: Protein has a high thermic effect, forcing the body to expend more calories during its breakdown and metabolism. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T006#GNS227_U4_T006_h5)

question: What does non-exercise activity thermogenesis (NEAT) mean in daily life?

options.A: Energy used only during scheduled gym workouts
options.B: Calories burned through everyday movements like walking and fidgeting
options.C: Resting calories used by the heart while sleeping
options.D: Heat generated by a fever during an infection

explanation: NEAT is a fancy term for a simple idea: it's all the calories you burn just moving around during your normal day, outside of going to the gym! [learn more](GNS227_U4_T006#GNS227_U4_T006_h5)

question: What happens to the body during a state of positive energy balance?

options.A: It maintains a completely stable body weight
options.B: It burns stored fat to make up for a calorie deficit
options.C: It stores extra calories and gains weight
options.D: It stops all metabolic processes to save energy

explanation: When you take in more calories than you burn, the extra energy gets stored, primarily as fat, leading to weight gain. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T006#GNS227_U4_T006_h6)

question: A patient is recovering from major surgery and needs tissue repair. Which energy state is best?
explanation: Healing takes work! Building new cells and repairing tissues require extra building blocks and calories, so a positive energy balance is just what the patient needs. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T006#GNS227_U4_T006_h6)

question: What does indirect calorimetry measure to calculate energy use?

options.B: Total body heat in a sealed room
options.C: Oxygen consumption and carbon dioxide production

explanation: Spot on! Indirect calorimetry figures out how many calories someone is burning by analyzing the gases they breathe in and out. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T006#GNS227_U4_T006_h7)

question: Why are predictive equations used in hospital wards instead of direct calorimetry?

options.A: Calorimetry machines do not measure oxygen
options.B: Formulas are practical and easy to calculate using basic measurements
options.C: Calorimetry chambers are required by law
options.D: Equations are always 100% error-free for everyone

explanation: Using formulas gives nurses a fast, helpful estimate without needing complex or expensive test equipment right at the bedside. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T006#GNS227_U4_T006_h7)

question: What is a major risk of overfeeding a critically ill patient on a ventilator?

options.A: Extra carbon dioxide production making it harder to breathe off the ventilator
options.B: Total elimination of the need for IV fluids
options.D: A sudden drop in blood sugar levels

explanation: Giving too many calories—especially from carbs—makes the body produce extra carbon dioxide. This makes breathing much harder for a patient trying to come off a ventilator! [learn more](GNS227_U4_T006#GNS227_U4_T006_h8)

question: As a nurse, what is your most critical intervention to catch energy imbalances early in hospitalized patients?

options.B: Performing regular and accurate weight measurements
options.C: Asking the patient their favorite food

explanation: You've got this! Tracking weight trends over time is the most reliable way for a nurse to see if a patient's calorie intake is matching what their body needs. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T006#GNS227_U4_T006_h8)
